terms.gloss: a mood of the verb; in Quintilian also a voice
evidence: Quint. 1.5.41: fīunt soloecismī per genera, tempora, persōnās, modōs
terms.comment: The question is Cujus modī est?, in what mood is it? (Traupman 240). Quintilian also calls the passive patiendī modus (9.3.7). Traupman’s classroom dialogue, in the manner of the Roman school grammars, counts five (indicative, subjunctive, imperative, infinitive, impersonal); modern grammars count three (Traupman 225).

phrases.latin: ideōque in eō fīunt soloecismī per genera, tempora, persōnās, modōs
phrases.english: and so in the verb mistakes happen in voice, tense, person and mood
In what mood is it? — The indicative.
the subjunctive mood, e.g. “although I read”

sources: Lewis & Short: modus
